fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled DER certificate reaches SAN extension parsing; cur points to the embedded subject_alt_names field of the mbedtls_x509_crt struct.
First SAN entry is a valid dNSName (tag 0x82); mbedtls_x509_parse_subject_alt_name succeeds and sets cur->buf.p to the data pointer.
Since cur->buf.p is non-NULL, a new heap node is allocated and cur advances to it; subject_alt_name->next now points to this heap allocation.
Second SAN entry is a malformed otherName (tag 0xa0) with HW_MODULE_NAME OID but truncated payload; x509_get_other_name returns MBEDTLS_ERR_X509_INVALID_EXTENSIONS, not FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE.

fine_trace.code: mbedtls_x509_sequence *seq_cur = subject_alt_name->next; while( seq_cur != NULL ) { seq_prv = seq_cur; seq_cur = seq_cur->next; mbedtls_free( seq_prv ); }
fine_trace.note: Error path frees the allocated node(s) but does NOT set subject_alt_name->next = NULL; the field remains a dangling pointer to freed heap memory.

fine_trace.code: ret = x509_get_crt_ext( &p, end, crt ); if( ret != 0 ) { mbedtls_x509_crt_free( crt ); return( ret ); }
fine_trace.note: x509_get_crt_ext propagates the SAN parse error; x509_crt_parse_der_core calls mbedtls_x509_crt_free(crt) on the error path.
